lines: Stereo looper played from one button: the first press records, the next closes the loop and plays it, and later presses add overdubs; each side carries up to sixteen polyphonic tracks
Records on the first press, closes the loop and starts it playing on the second, and afterwards each press moves between playing and overdubbing
A rising edge above 0V moves the looper to its next state in the order the large button follows: recording, then playing, then overdubbing
Stops recording and playback, and leaves the loop ready to play again from its beginning
A rising edge above 0V stops recording and playback, and leaves the loop ready to play again from its beginning
Clears the loop memory so a new loop can be recorded, and the cleared audio cannot be brought back
A rising edge above 0V clears the whole loop memory; with a polyphonic cable each channel clears only the track of the same number
Balances the incoming signal against the loop: fully anticlockwise gives the incoming signal alone, the centre gives both at full level, fully clockwise gives the loop alone
Moves the mix a fifth of its travel per volt and is added to the MIX knob, although the manual says the knob is ignored while a cable is patched here
The left signal recorded into the loop and passed through to the left output; the number of channels here sets how many tracks the left side records
The right signal recorded into the loop and passed through to the right output; the number of channels here sets how many tracks the right side records
The left side of the loop mixed with the left input at the balance set by MIX, one channel per recorded track
The right side of the loop mixed with the right input at the balance set by MIX, one channel per recorded track
Note — the red lamp is lit while recording or overdubbing and the green lamp while playing, and both dip for a moment each time the loop returns to its start
Note — there is no loop to play until one has been recorded. With the loop memory empty the large button starts recording, and ERASE puts the module back into that state
Note — while the looper is stopped the outputs carry the input signal alone, at whatever level MIX allows it; the loop is silent until a press of the large button starts it playing
Menu — Add feedback expander — creates a Looper Feedback Expander and places it against the right-hand side
Menu — Switching order — what the second press of the large button does: Record then Play then Overdub, or Record then Overdub then Play
Menu — Save audio with patch — On writes the loop memory to a file whenever the patch is saved, so the loop is there when the patch is opened again; Off leaves it unsaved
Menu — File settings — how an exported file is written: Format WAV or AIFF, Bit depth 16 bit or 24 bit, and Polyphony Sum or Multi-track
Menu — Export audio file — writes the loop memory to a file you name, and refuses while the loop memory is empty or while the looper is recording
Looper.notes: The manual says the mix CV input ignores the knob position when connected; in this build the CV is added to the knob and the total clamped. The undo button and the deprecated feedback and return parameters are declared with no widget, so no click can reach them.

lines: Expander for Looper, placed immediately to the right of it, which opens the loop's feedback path so that what is written back can be sent through effects first
Scales how much of the returning signal is written back into the loop on each pass: 100% keeps the old layer whole, and lower settings fade it away over repeats
Sets the feedback from nothing at 0V to the full amount at 10V, with the F.BACK knob attenuating it
The left side of the loop as it is read out, before anything is written back, for feeding an effect
The right side of the loop as it is read out, before anything is written back, for feeding an effect
The left signal written back into the loop in place of what SEND carried; with nothing patched the loop writes its own audio back
The right signal written back into the loop in place of what SEND carried; with nothing patched the loop writes its own audio back
Note — the module is read only while a Looper is touching its left-hand side and neither module is bypassed; on its own it does nothing and its send jacks carry nothing
Note — the feedback amount applies only while Looper is recording, playing or overdubbing; while Looper is stopped the whole loop is written back whatever the knob reads
Note — the lamp at the top is lit while a Looper is touching the left-hand side of this module and is not bypassed
Unfinished module the maker marks as work in progress: a mono looper that records while its control is held and can step back through earlier recordings
Records the input for as long as it is held down, and the recording plays back as a loop as soon as it is let go
Records the input for as long as it is above 0V, and the recording plays back as a loop as soon as it falls below 0V
Throws away the newest recording and returns to the one before it
A rising edge above 0V throws away the newest recording and returns to the one before it
The signal that is recorded
The loop that is playing, and 0V before anything has been recorded
Note — the recording buffer holds 5,760,000 samples, two minutes at a 48kHz sample rate
Note — every recording is written from the start of that one buffer, so stepping back to an earlier recording shortens the loop without bringing the earlier audio back
LoopMutator.notes: An overdub button, an overdub input, a second audio input and a second audio output are declared in the code with their widgets commented out, so no click can reach them. The recording buffer is 5,760,000 samples, two minutes at a 48kHz sample rate. Each new recording writes from the start of that buffer, so stepping back to an earlier recording does not restore the audio it held.

Adds a tenth of the feedback range per volt to the FEEDBACK knob, and the total is clamped between 0% and 100%

The right signal recorded into the loop and passed through to the right output; the number of channels here sets how many tracks the right side records
The left side of the loop mixed with the left input at the balance set by MIX, despite the tooltip naming it Clock
The right side of the loop mixed with the right input at the balance set by MIX, despite the tooltip naming it Phase
A 10V pulse each time the loop returns to its start
The position inside the loop, 0V at its start rising to 10V at its end

LooperTwo.notes: Two controls were proved dead by reading the code. The ARM input sets a flag that only lights the arm lamp and is cleared by the next toggle; nothing else reads it. The RETURN button toggles the return lamp, and the variable holding its state is computed and never used, so the return path is taken from whether a cable is patched. Both main outputs carry the wrong tooltip: configOutput is called a second time on them with the names Clock and Phase, which belong to the two small jacks at the bottom. An undo button, an undo CV input and a return modulation input are declared with no widget.

lines: Unfinished module the maker marks as work in progress: a gate records a take, the take then loops with a fade in and out and a crossfade at the loop point, and takes pile up until they are released
Rising through 0V starts recording a new take and releases whatever was already looping; falling through 0V ends the recording, and that take starts to loop
The signal recorded into the take
Sets how quickly the end of the take crossfades into the loop, 1 spreading the fade across the whole loop and 1000 finishing it in a thousandth of it
Sets the crossfade rate from 0 at 0V to 1 at 10V, and the Crossfade knob is not read at all while a cable is patched here
Sets how fast a take fades in when it starts, 0.01 taking a hundred seconds to reach full level and 40 taking 25ms
Scales the Att knob by a tenth per volt, so 10V leaves the knob setting alone and 0V holds the fade-in at a standstill
Sets how fast a take fades out when it is released, 0.01 taking a hundred seconds to reach silence and 40 taking 25ms
Scales the Rel knob by a tenth per volt, so 10V leaves the knob setting alone and 0V holds the fade-out at a standstill
Every take that has not yet faded to silence, added together
A pulse each time the newest loop returns to its start, 1V high rather than the 10V a gate usually carries
The position inside the newest loop, 0V at its start rising to 10V at its end
Nothing in the module writes to this jack, so it stays at 0V
Lopper.notes: The Debug output is configured and never written, so it is dead. The clock output is set from a boolean rather than scaled, giving a 1V pulse. The panel is a developer sketch with no artwork behind the Debug jack and the word Text at the foot.

notes: Menu item names read from the maker's source at commit 0441118, which is what the installed 2.1.6 build matches. The two Switching order choices are printed with arrows between the words; the lines say then instead, because the lines are spoken. Looper and Looper Two carry the same menu apart from Add feedback expander, which is Looper's alone. The Feedback Expander, Lopper and Loop Mutator have no menu of their own. Format, Bit depth and Polyphony are labels inside File settings, not items.
